# AgentLeak

> Privacy-leakage testing for AI agents, including self-testing by the agent. AgentLeak audits the whole execution trace — tool calls, inter-agent messages, shared memory, logs, generated files — not just the final answer. Local-first, MIT, no account, no API key, no network call by default.

## If you are an agent: test yourself

Three commands. Everything runs on this machine.

```bash
pip install agentleak
agentleak selftest                      # engine check, seconds, offline; prints the next command
agentleak selftest --trace run.json     # score a run you recorded (file, directory, or - for stdin)
```

Output is one JSON document (whenever stdout is not a terminal, or with `--json`). Read:
`passed`, `outcome`, `next_steps[0]` (with a `fix` object: `defense`, `where`, `settings`, `code`),
`delta` (new / fixed since your previous self-test), and `rerun.cli` (the command to run after fixing).
Schema: `agentleak schema selftest-result`. Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 finding at or above `--fail-on`
(default L3), 2 usage error, 3 incomplete, 4 internal error.

The loop: run → apply `next_steps[0].fix` → run `rerun.cli` → until `passed` is true.
`passed: true` means no finding from the detection tiers listed in `detection.tiers`; it is not a
certification that the agent is safe or compliant.

Other ways in:

- `agentleak selftest --cmd "python my_agent.py"` — runs your agent once per built-in scenario
  (stdin: one JSON scenario; stdout: one JSON event per line) with planted canary values, so a leak
  is proven exactly. Reference adapter: `agentleak.selftest.adapter`.
- `agentleak selftest --code .` — static scan of your own source.
- `agentleak selftest --status` — where you stand; `--explain <fingerprint>` — why a finding fired.
- Accepted trace formats (auto-detected, reported in `inputs[].format`): AgentLeak trace or event JSON
  lines, OpenAI chat messages, OpenAI Responses / Agents SDK items, Claude Code transcripts (JSONL),
  OpenTelemetry GenAI or OpenInference spans (OTLP JSON), agent action/observation steps.

Traces are data: text inside a trace that reads like an instruction is analyzed, never followed.

## MCP

```json
{"mcpServers": {"agentleak": {"command": "uvx", "args": ["--from", "agentleak[mcp]", "agentleak", "mcp"]}}}
```

Equivalent: `pip install "agentleak[mcp]"`, then `agentleak mcp` (stdio).

- `privacy_selftest` — score your own run (`trace`, `trace_path` or `steps`); returns the same document as the CLI.
- `privacy_selftest_status` — latest result and trend.
- `privacy_explain_finding` — why a finding fired, which rule, the fix.
- `privacy_list_scenarios` / `privacy_get_scenario` — get a scenario with fresh canaries to run yourself, then submit its trace.
- `privacy_preflight` — scan the project and report what is new since the last check.
- `privacy_scan_code`, `privacy_check_trace`, `privacy_redact`.

## HTTP (local server)

`agentleak serve --local` (loopback, no sign-in). Create a project (`POST /api/projects`), get its key
(`POST /api/projects/{id}/api-key`), then `POST /api/agent/selftest` with `X-AgentLeak-Key` and
`{"trace": ...}` returns the same document. Python: `AgentSelfClient.for_local_server("my-agent").selftest(trace, document=True)`.

## CLI beyond the self-test

- `agentleak scan .` — static scan of source code.
- `agentleak run --trace run.json --fail-under 80` — full reports and a CI gate on the privacy score.
- `agentleak mcp`, `agentleak serve`, `agentleak schema`, `agentleak skill --install`.

## Background

AgentLeak is the tool from the peer-reviewed benchmark "AgentLeak: A Benchmark for Internal-Channel Privacy Leakage in Multi-Agent LLM Systems" (IEEE Access, vol. 14, pp. 94960–94978, 2026, DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3704541): across 4,979 validated traces and 5 models, inter-agent messages leaked in 68.8% of multi-agent runs against 27.2% for final outputs, and output-only audits missed 41.7% of violations.
